reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes entering a Luna trade before a snapshot to pursue a new-token airdrop and presents possible gains of doubling or more as part of a time-sensitive buy-in pitch. The speaker also directs viewers to a Voyager referral and characterizes the resulting Luna exposure as zero-risk because of a Bitcoin reward offset. Although the speaker warns of a possible post-event drop and uncertainty about timing, the purchase suggestion and risk claim remain.

citations.quote: if you are thinking about getting in you may want to get in beforehand
you want to be able to buy it and sell it on a centralized exchange you can use the link for voyager in the description
If it does go up, there is absolutely the possibility that Terra Luna will go back down right afterwards.
anybody holding Luna at that point in time will be entitled to receive an airdrop of the new LUNA

Can it go up 10% in price? Absolutely. Can it double, triple, quadruple? Absolutely, but it depends on the amount of people and the amount of excitement surrounding this potential airdrop on the new Luna tokens.

opening.argument: This is framed as uncertain market commentary, not a promise of profit. The speaker expressly warns viewers to expect volatility and says the price could move much lower after the event. He also acknowledges that the snapshot timing and proposal details are unclear. Those qualifications materially change the message: viewers are being told to account for risk and incomplete information, not assured that buying will succeed. A conditional discussion of possible outcomes, accompanied by explicit downside warnings, is consistent with ordinary financial analysis rather than deceptive solicitation.

i i did it did not say the uh time zone when it was going to be or going to be happening there
i don't know what the exact proposal is
look forward to the 27th is being a very volatile day

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account emphasizes possible gains and the phrase “get in beforehand,” but it understates the surrounding warnings. The speaker directly identifies a possible immediate decline and repeatedly presents volatility as the central risk. Mentioning a trading possibility while warning that the event may move sharply in either direction does not establish a deceptive guarantee or concealment of risk.

citations.quote: If it does go up, there is absolutely the possibility that Terra Luna will go back down right afterwards.
if you are thinking about getting in you may want to get in beforehand
look forward to the 27th is being a very volatile day

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings do not erase the actionable timing recommendation. The speaker pairs uncertainty with an invitation to enter before the snapshot, while also discussing doubling, tripling, or quadrupling. A disclaimer can describe downside without making the underlying buy-in pitch non-deceptive; the practical message still encourages a time-sensitive purchase based on a speculative event.

opening.argument: The video's core activity is explaining a market event and its possible trading effects. It distinguishes a conventional blockchain fork from a new blockchain, then explains how a snapshot could relate to an airdrop and why buying pressure might change around that event. The presentation includes competing scenarios: a rise from anticipated demand, a sell-off after the snapshot, or no meaningful volatility. That is explanatory market commentary about an event and its mechanics, rather than certification that viewers will profit.

citations.quote: forking is is when you take a cryptocurrency and you fork off the blockchain and the new cryptocurrency holds all of the history
It is basically a Luna 2.0 or a new Luna coin using a new blockchain that has no association whatsoever with the current Luna.
during that block, when that block is solved, anybody holding Luna at that point in time will be entitled to receive an airdrop of the new LUNA
if it doesn't happen if the volatility doesn't happen, great. At least you are prepared for it

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the discussion analysis does not make it a purchase solicitation. The video explains the distinction between the old and new blockchains, describes the snapshot mechanics, and asks viewers whether they plan to hold through it. Its alternative scenarios and discussion of post-snapshot selling show an attempt to analyze market behavior, not a simple instruction that profit is assured.

citations.quote: That is not the proposal that is going to be happening with Luna.
anybody holding Luna at that point in time will be entitled to receive an airdrop of the new LUNA
whether or not you guys plan on holding through the snapshot

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The mechanics explanation is used to support a concrete entry thesis. The speaker says people may buy immediately before the snapshot, predicts possible gains as high as fourfold, and asks whether viewers need to get in now. That combination goes beyond neutral education: it turns the explanation into a time-sensitive trading pitch, even though the outcomes are stated conditionally.

citations.quote: We can see them flock in right before that block is solved.
Can it go up 10% in price? Absolutely. Can it double, triple, quadruple? Absolutely
Do you think that on the 27th, the price is going to be driven so much higher that you need to get in now?

opening.argument: The commercial element is an ordinary platform referral embedded in investing commentary, not evidence of a scam mechanism. The speaker names an exchange, describes a promotional Bitcoin reward, and says viewers can use the link to obtain it. The supplied material does not show a credential request, downline-income scheme, or guaranteed return; instead, the offer is presented as a conventional referral incentive alongside discussion of buying and selling. Even the risk characterization is tied to a limited promotional amount, not a promise that Terra Luna itself cannot lose value.

citations.quote: you can use the link for Voyager in the description. You're gonna get $25 in free Bitcoin
if you want a zero-risk exposure, just get that $25 in Bitcoin and have a $25 exposure to Terra Luna
if it goes to zero, clearly the Terra 25 is gonna offset it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The referral mention is a standard promotional aside, and the speaker does not claim that the underlying token is risk-free. He separately warns that the token could fall sharply after the snapshot. The presence of an exchange link and a stated reward therefore does not establish a fraudulent mechanism or transform the broader market discussion into a scam.

citations.quote: You're gonna get $25 in free Bitcoin
we can see the price go down ten twenty thirty forty fifty percent
If it does go up, there is absolutely the possibility that Terra Luna will go back down right afterwards.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The referral is not isolated from the trading pitch: it gives viewers a route to buy the promoted asset while describing the reward as offsetting a total loss and calling the exposure zero-risk. The later volatility warning does not cure that risk characterization, and ordinary referral formatting does not make a speculative purchase recommendation safe or non-deceptive.
